newsitem.title: CHINA: Asian traders see LME lead rising in short term.
newsitem.headline: Asian traders see LME lead rising in short term.

text.p: Asian metals traders expect lead prices on the London Metal Exchange (LME) to continue to rise in the short term, but said a correction is likely before the end of March because the current rally is technical.
Lead prices on the LME ended the Friday afternoon kerb at $698 a tonne, up $23 a tonne from the Thursday close.
Options-related buying, fund short-covering and tight April dates were responsible for the metal's dramatic surge, which hit a high of $705 in the afternoon kerb, London traders said.
Ahead of next Wednesday's options declaration, open interest was concentrated on $725.
"There is no fundamental reason, only technical reasons" for the rally in LME lead prices, said Vinod Kumar, managing director of Donald Mcarthy in Singapore.
He said he expected the LME price to head above $750 a tonne in Monday trading.
"But once this options-related activity is over then it should disappear altogether and then it (the lead price) should come back to, say, $650" by the end of March, Kumar told Reuters.
LME lead was trading in Asia at $699/705 a tonne, he said.
Copper remained a China play, traders in China, Hong Kong and Singapore said.
LME copper remains high, with traders in the region putting it down to market anticipation of Chinese buying.
Traders polled by Reuters said China would not come into the market at the current high prices, but would prefer to wait until prices come down below $2,200 a tonne.
In Friday trading on the LME, copper intially dipped to a low of $2,363 a tonne, from Thursday's kerb close of $2,393, after LME stocks fell by an expected 3,475 tonnes.
Donald Mcarthy's Kumar said he expected to see a further drop in LME copper stocks when figures are released on Tuesday of 2,000 to 2,500 tonnes.
Aluminium would also fall, he said, by 6,000 to 7,000 tonnes.
